question: The mink tribe uses words like yugara, or agara, or yutia, right? It seems they are used when addressing somebody, but is there any idea behind it? Please tell me. On this occasion, please "Garuchuu" me. (Laughs) Disciple Mag
answer: Garuchuu. Yes. I think this might be confusing at first, but it's simple. ["aitsu" Male "agara"/Female "atia"[T/L: He/She (over there): Derives from ano yatsu] · "soitsu" Male "sogara"/Female "soita"[T/L: He/She (close to the speaking person): Derives from sono yatsu] · "yatsu" Male "yagara"/Female "yatia"[T/L: He/She (general)] · "anata" Male "yugara"/Female "yutia"[T/L: You (more formal)]] That's basically it. Additionally, plural forms would be "yugara-ra" and so on. Please read it spontaneously. It's a miracle how a species, living in an isolated country, can communicate with words like this.
name: Jinbei's Disciple Mag
